label: Calorie tracker app
text: I'm making a calorie and macro tracker app for phones. I use Claude Code. I don't really know what I need.

items.text: A phone app where people log meals and track calories and macros
items.quote: calorie and macro tracker app for phones

items.text: You're not sure yet what you need
items.quote: I don't really know what I need

concepts.term: phone app for iPhone and Android
keeping Claude Code on track between sessions

needs.reason: Only if you add barcode scanning, which you didn't mention: Open Food Facts is a free database of packaged foods your app can look up by barcode.
Claude Code already covers this: it reads a CLAUDE.md notes file at the start of every session, and /init writes a starter one. Nothing to add.

expo-app-toolkit.why: You're making a tracker app for phones and aren't sure what you need. Expo is the usual way to build one app that runs on both iPhone and Android.
expo-app-toolkit.how_it_helps: Claude Code gets Expo's own setup guides and can start test builds, so you can try the app on your phone early without learning native code.
expo-app-toolkit.do_you_need_it: It's the first step, unless you have already picked another way to build the app. The other picks plug into it.
expo-app-toolkit.skip_if: Skip it if the app is already written natively in Swift or Kotlin, or in Flutter.
expo-app-toolkit.summary: Expo's official add-on for Claude Code: guides, test builds and app store help for phone apps.

usda-fooddata-central.why: A calorie and macro tracker needs nutrition numbers for every food people log, and typing them in by hand doesn't scale.
usda-fooddata-central.how_it_helps: Your app can search a free government food database and fill in calories, protein, carbs and fat as people log meals.
usda-fooddata-central.do_you_need_it: You need it unless people will type in their own numbers.
usda-fooddata-central.skip_if: Skip it if you already have a food database, or people will enter their own numbers.
usda-fooddata-central.summary: The US Department of Agriculture's FoodData Central: a free food and nutrient database with a free sign-up key.

supabase-backend.why: A tracker keeps each person's meals and goals. If people sign in or switch phones, that log has to live somewhere online.
supabase-backend.how_it_helps: Claude Code can set up sign-in and a database for food logs and goals, and check them for you, through Supabase's own add-on.
supabase-backend.do_you_need_it: If the log stays only on the phone, it can wait.
supabase-backend.skip_if: Skip it if the data stays on the phone, or you already use another online database.
supabase-backend.summary: Supabase's official add-on for Claude Code: a hosted database with sign-in, managed from your AI tool.

sentry-crash-alerts.why: You didn't mention crash reports. Once testers or real users have the app, it helps to hear when it breaks on their phones.
sentry-crash-alerts.how_it_helps: Crashes on testers' phones show up with the line that failed, and Claude Code can read those reports to help fix them.
sentry-crash-alerts.do_you_need_it: Useful later, once other people start using the app. The free plan covers one person.
sentry-crash-alerts.skip_if: Skip it if you already use a crash reporter, or nobody else uses the app yet.
sentry-crash-alerts.summary: Sentry's official add-on: crash reporting for your app, plus a way for Claude Code to read the reports.
